title: The Complete Guide to Telegram Bot API Free (2026)
meta_description: What does Telegram Bot API Free cost in 2026 (spoiler: nothing), and how do you set it up properly? Covers free tiers, open-source alternatives and honest…
intro: You don't need a budget to get good at telegram bot api free. You need a map of the free tools, and an honest read on the trade-offs between them. Here's that map — researched, written and fact-checked by the same engine that publishes this blog.

We'll walk through Telegram Bot API, Mastodon API, Bluesky At Protocol, and Automate the boring parts — and finish with the questions people actually ask, so you can check before you buy anything. You shouldn't have to buy anything.

sections.heading: Telegram Bot API
paragraphs: First, the thing that actually matters: The Telegram Bot API is free, HTTP-based and needs nothing but a token from @BotFather.

In practice that means: Create a bot in one message, then send and receive messages, create channels, and drive webhooks entirely over plain HTTPS. It is the cheapest 'social media' channel a self-publishing site can own, and this blog posts to it when a token is configured.
For a personal project or side business, this covers you without breaking a sweat.
bullets: Message @BotFather and /newbot to get a token
Optionally set a webhook with setWebhook for incoming events

sections.heading: Mastodon API
paragraphs: Worth spending ten minutes on: Mastodon's API is free and fully documented — any instance lets you register an app and post programmatically.

In other words: Create an app in your instance's developer settings, exchange it for a token, and the REST API handles statuses, follows and search. Because the whole platform is open source and federated, posting to it costs nothing and can point at an instance you run yourself.
Keep it this simple and you'll be ahead of most tutorials out there.

sections.heading: Bluesky At Protocol
paragraphs: Skip the fluff and start here: Bluesky runs on the open AT Protocol, whose public API is free — an account plus an app password is all a bot needs to post.

In other words: createSession returns an access token, and app.bsky.feed.post publishes a post. No middleman, no paid 'basic tier' for your own account's posting, and the protocol is openly specified so the implementation is boring in the best way.
The links in the sources section go straight to the primary docs.

sections.heading: Automate the boring parts
paragraphs: First, the thing that actually matters: Anything you do twice by hand should become a script. That's the entire discipline of free automation.

Which, in day-to-day terms, means: A cron expression, a webhook, or a scheduled workflow costs nothing to run and buys back an hour every week. Start with one small automation — a nightly backup, a feed check, a deploy on push — and add more only when the first one proves itself.
For a personal project or side business, this covers you without breaking a sweat.
